clues: Walt and whoever took the binoculars are two different people: one signed the slate at noon, the other at 11:00 a.m.
Of the tide chart's borrower and the person who signed at noon, one wore ski gloves and the other wore fleece gloves.
Gus signed the slate exactly two hours after Amara did.
Whoever wore the leather gloves signed the slate later than Amara.
Between Selma and whoever took the spare key, one wore fingerless gloves and the other wore fleece.
The visitor who signed at 11:30 a.m. wore either fingerless or wool gloves.
Whoever borrowed the megaphone signed the slate earlier than Walt.
hints: Look at clue 3. Which two sign-out times are exactly two hours apart? Then see where clue 1 leaves Walt.
Clue 5, a pair clue, leaves Selma just two glove choices. After clues 3 and 1, test one of them with a Suppose, then follow clue 2.
Suppose Selma wore fingerless. Then the spare key's borrower wore fleece (clue 5), Gus wore ski (clue 2), and the tide chart's borrower has no gloves left.
So Selma wore fleece and took the tide chart (clue 2). Clue 6 keeps fleece off 11:30 a.m., so Selma signed at 10:30 a.m.

solution.key_idea: Selma wore fingerless or fleece gloves; supposing fingerless leaves the tide chart's borrower no gloves at all, so she wore fleece.
steps: Clue 3 puts Amara at 10:00 a.m. and Gus at noon. Clue 1 then puts Walt at 11:00 a.m., and the binoculars with Gus.
By clue 2, Gus and the tide chart's borrower wore the ski and fleece gloves. By clue 5, Selma wore fingerless or fleece.
Suppose Selma wore fingerless. Then the spare key's borrower wore fleece (clue 5), so Gus (binoculars) wore ski, leaving the tide chart's borrower no gloves.
So Selma wore fleece, not fingerless. Gus wore ski, Selma took the tide chart (clue 2), and the spare key went with fingerless (clue 5).
Clue 6 keeps Selma's fleece off 11:30 a.m., so she signed at 10:30 a.m., and Teddy at 11:30 a.m.
Clue 4 keeps the leather gloves off Amara, and clue 6 keeps them off Teddy, so Walt wore leather.
Clue 7 puts the megaphone before Walt's 11:00 a.m. Selma's 10:30 a.m. went with the tide chart, so the megaphone was Amara's.
Walt's leather rules him out for the spare key, so Teddy took it, in fingerless gloves. Walt took the life ring; Amara wore wool.
solution.epilogue: Teddy signed out the spare key at 11:30 a.m., in fingerless gloves that left his fingers free for the camera. He wanted to photograph the Keeper's Lamp in the low winter light for his series.

answer_line: Teddy borrowed the spare lighthouse key.
